Healthcare Revenue Analytics

Turning Billing Data Into a Financial Playbook

Every claim your practice submits generates data: what was billed, what was paid, how long it took, and why it was denied if it was. Most of that data disappears into a billing system and never gets used. Revenue analytics is the discipline of pulling it back out, turning it into trends, comparisons and benchmarks that a practice owner can actually act on.

The value is in comparison, not just visibility. Knowing your denial rate is 8% means little on its own. Knowing it is 8% against a specialty benchmark of 5%, and that it is driven mostly by one payer's authorization requirements, is something a practice can actually fix.

PMEX turns every claim, payment and denial your practice generates into a comprehensive and interactive analytics dashboard, so decisions get made on current data instead of a gut feeling about how collections are going.

Financial KPIs

The Six Numbers Every Practice Should Track

Gross Collection Rate

Total collected against total charges billed.

Net Collection Rate

Total collected against the amount actually allowed by payers.

Days in A/R

Average time to collect after a claim is filed.

Denial Rate

Share of submitted claims that come back denied.

Clean Claim Rate

Claims accepted on first submission with no errors.

Cost to Collect

What it costs the practice, in staff and overhead, to collect each dollar billed.
